item.title: One dies as truck overturns in Lagos midnight crash
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni One person has died after a fully loaded Mercedes-Benz six-tyre truck overturned around the TREM axis of Gbagada, inward Oshodi, Lagos State, in a midnight accident. The deceased, an elderly man whose identity had yet to be established, was reportedly thrown out of the truck after one of its front tyres burst, causing the driver to lose control of the vehicle. The truck, with registration number ABJ 37 AC, was conveying assorted consignments, including sealed bags and newly branded event chairs, when the incident occurred. According to reports, the vehicle was travelling at considerable speed when the tyre burst. In the ensuing struggle to stabilise the truck, the passenger seated in the front cabin was flung out and hit his head against a sharp object, resulting in his instant death. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) said its Night Rescue Team, which was conducting surveillance along major traffic corridors, promptly mobilised to the scene and cordoned off the accident site. The operatives subsequently evacuated the deceased from the busy carriageway into an ambulance operated by the Lagos State Emergency Medical Services (LASEMS), to prevent further exposure to approaching motorists and avert another accident. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed condolences to the family of the deceased, describing the incident as a painful and avoidable loss that underscored the dangers of poor road safety practices. Bakare-Oki said the rescue and traffic management operations received support from personnel of the Pedro Police Division, who provided security, and officers of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, who assisted with emergency response. He explained that the overturned truck could not be immediately recovered because of the volume and nature of its cargo. Arrangements were therefore made to transfer the consignments into another empty truck before recovering the vehicle. The LASTMA boss condemned excessive speeding, warning that it reduces drivers’ reaction time, compromises vehicle stability and increases the severity of road crashes, particularly when unexpected mechanical failures occur. He said the consequences of the accident could have been less severe if the truck had been travelling at a controlled speed, despite the sudden tyre burst. Bakare-Oki urged heavy-duty vehicle operators, commercial transporters and other motorists to adopt responsible driving practices, conduct regular mechanical inspections and pay close attention to the condition of tyres, braking systems and other critical vehicle components before embarking on journeys. He also advised drivers to remain calm and apply appropriate vehicle-control techniques when confronted with sudden mechanical problems, warning that excessive speed could turn a manageable failure into a fatal incident. item.title: Liverpool return to winning ways with 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace
item.description: Florian Wirtz bagged his first Premier League goal this season as Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday. Andoni Iraola’s side erased the bitter taste of successive losses to Arsenal and Fenerbahce with a comfortable victory at Selhurst Park. Alexis Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead late in the first half before Wirtz, whose last league goal came against the same opponents in April, doubled the Reds’ advantage nine minutes into the second half. Alexander Isak netted Liverpool’s third in the 89th minute before Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty for bottom of the table Palace. Liverpool are up to fourth place after their fourth away league win this season. It was a much-needed success for Iraola, who had started to hear some awkward questions about Liverpool’s inconsistent run in his first season in charge after arriving from Bournemouth to replace the sacked Arne Slot. Yeremy Pino went agonisingly close to opening the scoring for Palace in the 18th minute when he curled against the bar. Palace striker Jorgen Strand Larsen had the ball in the back of Alisson Becker’s net in the 33rd minute. But his celebrations were cut short by the offside flag and a subsequent VAR check. Mac Allister made Palace pay for those misses in the 40th minute, nodding home a Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick in clinical fashion. Wirtz increased Liverpool’s advantage in the 54th minute, guiding a low Bradley Barcola cross into the bottom corner. Palace had a huge chance with just under 15 minutes remaining when Pino was denied by Alisson, who then saved from Jefferson Lerma before Nketiah lashed over. Sweden striker Isak put the result beyond doubt in the 89th minute with a deflected close-range strike. Palace earned a penalty after Dario Osorio clashed heads with Milos Kerkez but Nketiah’s goal was no consolation for under-fire Eagles boss Pierre Sage. item.title: Anambra begins reconstruction of failed roads ahead of Christmas
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Contractors handling major road projects in Anambra State have returned to site to reconstruct failed sections of the roads following a directive by the state government ahead of the forthcoming Christmas season. The development followed concerns over the failure of some portions of the roads, including sections that are yet to be officially commissioned. The affected projects include the Amawbia-Agulu-Ekwulobia-Uga dual carriageway, the Agulu-Nnewi dual carriageway and other major roads across the state. The Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Okey Ezeobi, had attributed the failures to extreme rainfall and flash flooding rather than the use of substandard construction materials. He, however, directed the contractors to undertake major reconstruction of the affected sections instead of carrying out temporary, spot repairs, in line with Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s emphasis on quality infrastructure delivery. Barely 12 hours after the directive, the contractors reportedly mobilised to their respective sites, with reconstruction work commencing across the state. At the Amawbia end of the dual carriageway, asphalt on one lane had been completely removed, while sand-filling work was ongoing. Similar activities were observed at the Neni section of the Agulu-Nnewi road and along the Nnewi-Ozubulu-Okija dual carriageway. During a visit to some of the project sites at the weekend, officials of the Ministry of Works were seen monitoring the progress of the reconstruction. Ezeobi had earlier dismissed allegations that the road failures resulted from poor construction, insisting that the contractors engaged by the state government were reputable companies capable of undertaking corrective work. “Because of the quality of these contractors, they are able to return to site to effect reconstruction whenever there is any failure and they do this at no cost to the state. “If we had given the contract to small companies, they won’t come back to address the failures. We took time to select all the contractors working for us,” he said. The commissioner attributed the affected portions to the impact of natural disasters, recalling that the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) had earlier issued warnings about possible flooding during the year. He explained that roads located in flood-prone areas were particularly vulnerable, citing sections of the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway where swamps and underground water movements had contributed to the damage. “Roads along flood-prone areas in the state are adversely affected. For instance, the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway is erosion-prone as there are swamps in some areas and the water there is always struggling to come up. “So in the affected places, we will remove the asphalt and do cement-based stabilisation to help suppress further underground water coming up to destroy it,” he said. item.title: Bauchi police arrest two suspected armed robbers, recover motorcycle
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two suspected armed robbers and recovered a stolen motorcycle and other valuables following a machete attack on two residents of the state. The suspects, alongside a third accomplice who is still at large, allegedly attacked a 26-year-old man at his residence in the Rafin Makaranta area of Bauchi metropolis in the early hours of November 6, 2026, inflicting machete injuries on his head. The attackers, reportedly armed with machetes, also dispossessed the victim and his friend, a resident of Makera area, of a motorcycle, two mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, power banks, an MP3 player, perfume and N45,000 cash. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday in Bauchi. Habib said operatives attached to the C Division responded to the incident and launched a manhunt for the perpetrators, leading to the arrest of two suspects on November 7. He identified the suspects as Uzairu Rabiu, alias Gwano, of Zawiyya area, Bauchi, and Hafizu Abdullahi, alias Tora, of Gubi village, Bauchi. According to him, the operatives recovered a stolen Haojue motorcycle, two mobile phones and a Bluetooth device from the suspects. The police spokesman added that the injured victim was receiving treatment at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH), Bauchi, and his condition was steadily improving. He said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the third suspect and recover the remaining stolen items. Habib added that the arrested suspects would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their swift response and urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to the police. He warned criminal elements to desist from violent activities, assuring residents that the command would sustain its operations to tackle armed robbery and other criminal activities across the state. item.title: ‎Labour demands immediate start to new Minimum Wage talks
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ ‎ABUJA— THE Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has accused the Federal Government of ignoring the statutory timetable for the next national minimum wage review, insisting that negotiations should already be under way rather than waiting until 2027. ‎ ‎NLC Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, speaking to Vanguard in Abuja, said the current N70,000 minimum wage was agreed on July 28, 2024 and backdated to May 1, 2024, but argued that the backdating did not alter the three-year review cycle introduced by the 2024 amendment to the Minimum Wage Act. ‎ ‎“In our estimation, the negotiations ought to have been on the way, or ought to be on the way, because one, the economic realities have since wiped out the value of the ₦70,000, upon which the minimum wage was premised,” Upah said. ‎ ‎He said the 2023 amendment changed only two things: the wage figure, from ₦30,000 to ₦70,000, and the review cycle, from five years to three years, adding that neither change authorised government or labour to shift the commencement date of the three-year cycle at will. ‎ ‎“The principal act was not amended, and there was nothing in the amended items that states that the three yearly cycle can be abridged by either of the parties. ‎ ‎“It is clear that this thing runs on the three yearly cycle now. It is like the constitution says a governor shall hold office for four years, and the governor has to hold office for four years.” ‎ ‎Upah argued that, on the NLC’s reading of the law, the three-year period should be counted from the earlier wage cycle, meaning negotiations ought to have started in June. He said the NLC had already alerted government to that position. ‎ ‎He said: “But if you want to follow the government logic, which is actually an error, that because it took effect from May, that the three years will start from May, if you follow that logic, the negotiations ought to start in November, because the act talks about starting six months before the process. ‎ ‎“So, in our view, there is no reason to do tomorrow what can be done today.” ‎ ‎The NLC scribe said the process of reviewing the minimum wage was lengthy and required hearings, consultations, a cost-of-living assessment and engagement with social partners. ‎ ‎According to him: “It is important for us to start early. Why must we run on a deficit calendar when we knew full well that this thing was going to start on a so-so date? It speaks to our state of unpreparedness.” ‎ ‎His position comes amid an ongoing dispute over when the next review should begin. The Federal Government has maintained that the current N70,000 wage is due for review on June 1, 2027, while organised labour has demanded immediate preparations for a new negotiation. ‎ ‎Asked about suggestions by some labour leaders that the next minimum wage would commence in August 2027, Upah dismissed the claim sharply, saying: “Whichever union leader that made that comment clearly spoke out of ignorance, and acted in erro

item.title: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 to escape Premier League bottom
item.description: Sunderland hauled themselves off the bottom of the Premier League as Enzo Le Fee’s penalty earned a huge 1-0 win over Chelsea for embattled boss Regis Le Bris. The Frenchman was under pressure after a dismal 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday put his position in doubt ahead of an international break. Sunderland, though, bounced back for a huge three points thanks to two controversial penalty decisions. Chelsea were furious that Cole Palmer was not awarded a spot-kick for a foul by Luke O’Nien moments before the only goal of the game. A VAR review deemed the contact made was outside the area and therefore could not be overturned. Sunderland were awarded a penalty at the other end 10 minutes before half-time. The visitors were again aggrieved that Levi Colwill was adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey as both players grappled in their attempt to reach the ball. Le Fee dispatched the resulting spot-kick past Mike Penders and Sunderland held on for just a second league win of the season. Chelsea missed the presence of Joao Pedro up front as Palmer and Morgan Rogers were kept in check by the home side. A fourth defeat in 10 league games under Xabi Alonso leaves the Blues in fifth, two points outside the top four. item.description: …Accuses APC of using violence, courts to weaken opposition …Cites declining confidence in INEC, judiciary …Jerry Gana urges President to act as father of the nation, not partisan politician By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Interim National Working Committee, Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, has urged President Bola Tinubu to urgently address rising political tension and violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that Nigeria could descend into crisis if the situation is allowed to deteriorate. Turaki said attacks on opposition politicians, intimidation of voters and declining public confidence in electoral institutions were threatening the credibility of the elections, insisting that no political ambition was worth the survival of the country. He spoke at a press conference in Abuja, where he presented a statement titled, The Country Is Boiling; Can We Reduce the Temperature? The PDP’s Interim National Working Committee, accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of shrinking the political space, encouraging attacks on opposition parties and using the judiciary to undermine political competition. Drawing parallels with the First and Second Republics, Turaki warned that the suppression of opposition parties and manipulation of electoral processes had contributed to political instability and democratic collapse in Nigeria’s past. Citing Yiaga Africa’s third National Voting Intentions Survey, released on October 7, 2026, he said 84 per cent of Nigerians were willing to vote, but 61 per cent feared violence could keep them away from polling stations. Only 34 per cent expressed confidence in the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), while 63 per cent had little or no confidence in the judiciary’s ability to resolve electoral disputes fairly. The PDP chairman cited alleged attacks on supporters of Peter Obi, the ADC presidential campaign of Atiku Abubakar and activist Omoyele Sowore, including incidents in Delta, Sokoto and Ekiti states. He accused APC-linked operatives of being behind the incidents, while also alleging that opposition parties were being weakened through politically motivated court cases and voter intimidation. He further accused some public officials of threatening voters with displacement if they failed to support the APC, warning that such actions could undermine Nigerians’ freedom to choose their leaders. Comparing the political rhetoric of successive presidents, Turaki recalled former President Goodluck Jonathan’s declaration ahead of the 2015 election that his ambition was not worth the blood of any Nigerian. He contrasted this with former President Muhammadu Buhari’s controversial pre-election warning that the country would be soaked in blood if he was prevented from winning, and Tinubu’s reported remarks that elections were not a tea party and victory must be grabbed, snatched and run with. item.title: FG secures $200m World Bank funding to boost fish production
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has secured a $200 million World Bank-backed financing commitment to boost fish production across the country through state governments, as part of efforts to reduce import dependence and strengthen Nigeria’s aquaculture industry. The funding, to be made available to state governments as concessional loans, is expected to support investments in fisheries and aquaculture, expand production capacity and create opportunities for private-sector participation. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, disclosed this at a high-level executive training on the Aquaculture Investment Guide organised by the ministry in collaboration with the World Bank Group in Abuja. Oyetola, who was represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Marine and Blue Economy, Prof. Busayo Fakinlede, said the financing would help states unlock their fisheries potential and develop commercially viable aquaculture projects. The minister, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser, Bolaji Akinola, said the Federal Government was prioritising collaboration with state governments, investors and development partners to position Nigeria as a fish-sufficient nation. He said expanding domestic fish production had become imperative to address the widening gap between local supply and consumption. According to him, the involvement of state governments is critical to achieving the country’s fish production targets. “Fish is a pillar of food security, household nutrition and rural livelihoods. No nation can call itself food secure while it imports most of the fish it eats. Our ambition is to produce more, import less and, in time, become a net exporter. That ambition can be achieved only when every state plays its part,” he said. Under the proposed framework, states are expected to identify priority aquaculture value chains, assess investment opportunities, develop bankable projects and commit to measurable contributions towards national fish production. Oyetola said the executive training was designed to equip state policymakers and technical officials with the expertise to translate investment opportunities into viable projects. He said the programme would focus on business models, risk management, environmental safeguards and public-private partnerships. The minister commended the World Bank Group for its support for Nigeria’s marine and blue economy development, particularly in analytical studies, capacity building and the development of the Aquaculture Investment Guide. He also disclosed plans to convene a stakeholders’ roundtable after the training to strengthen engagement with state governments, investors and development partners and establish implementation arrangements for the financing initiative. Meanwhile, Fakinlede said the ministry had increased national fish production from 1.1 million tonnes to 1.4 million tonnes through interventions aimed at strengthening the sector. item.title: NAF redeploys senior officers, appoints new commanders
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has announced a major redeployment of senior officers, appointing new Air Officers Commanding (AOCs), Principal Staff Officers (PSOs) and commanders across its operational commands, training institutions and strategic establishments. The exercise, approved by the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, on November 7, 2026, takes effect from November 2026. Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement, saying the appointments cover the NAF Headquarters, operational commands, Defence Headquarters, training institutions and other strategic establishments. He said the exercise was designed to align leadership competencies and professional experience with the Service’s evolving operational and institutional priorities. At NAF Headquarters, AVM AK Ademuwagun has been appointed Chief of Transformation and Innovation; AVM IV Ajiboye, Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation; AVM PN Amadi, Chief of Air Intelligence; AVM NN Ananaba, Chief of Operations; AVM AH Bakari, Air Provost Marshal; AVM EE Efiom, Chief of Training; and AVM MS Ibrahim, Chairman, Air Expo and International Liaison. Other appointments at the headquarters include AVM AG Kehinde as Chief of Civil-Military Relations; AVM MA Sulaiman as Chief of Communications and Information Systems; AVM S Peters as Coordinator, Project Implementation Team; and AVM AJ Laoye as Chief of Aircraft Engineering. AVM AY Dari becomes General Manager, Nigerian Air Force Investment Limited Group of Companies, while AVM NS Okoro has been appointed Director-General, AFRDI. New operational commanders At the operational command level, AVM NI Ilo has been appointed Air Officer Commanding, Tactical Air Command; AVM BR Mamman, AOC, Mobility Command; AVM OS Ogunsina, AOC, Logistics Command; AVM MN Onyebashi, AOC, Special Operations Command; and AVM FCS Nwakara, AOC, Ground Training Command. To strengthen operational command structures, AVM JI Ukeh has been appointed Commander, Nigerian Air Defence Corps. Other command appointments include AVM OA Abu as Chief of Staff, Mobility Command; AVM I Subi as Chief of Staff, Special Operations Command; AVM NB Folaji as Chief of Staff, Tactical Air Command; AVM F Ekpah as Chief of Staff, Ground Training Command; AVM ES Odekina as Chief of Staff, Logistics Command; and AVM M Umar as Chief of Staff, Air Training Command. AVM GI Jibia has also been appointed Deputy Force Commander, Operation HADIN KAI. item.title: Navy uncovers 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has uncovered approximately 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude oil at illegal storage and refining sites in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The discoveries were made during two separate operations conducted on October 24 and November 7, 2026, by personnel of the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh under Operation Delta Sentinel. The Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operations followed credible intelligence on illegal petroleum storage and refining activities within the Orashi Forest and adjoining areas. According to him, the naval team, during the October 24 operation, discovered two crude oil storage sites containing four dugout pits, 29 sacks and a 25-litre keg, with an estimated 8,675 litres of suspected crude oil. He said a subsequent operation on November 7 led to the discovery of two illegal refining sites comprising two large and 36 small dugout pits, alongside other storage facilities containing an estimated 59,500 litres of suspected stolen crude oil. Folorunsho said the discovered petroleum products and associated items were handled in accordance with established procedures. He explained that the operations underscored the Navy’s sustained intelligence-led efforts under Operation Delta Sentinel to dismantle illegal petroleum storage and refining infrastructure, disrupt crude oil theft networks and deny criminal elements access to the nation’s natural resources. He added that the Navy would maintain operational pressure in identified areas of criminal activity to support the protection of critical oil and gas infrastructure and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining the operations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to combat crude oil theft, disrupt illegal refining activities and protect the nation’s maritime and economic interests. item.title: 2Baba thrills fans at Bongo Flava@30 festival
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Nigerian music icon, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, thrilled music fans in Mbeya, Tanzania, with an energetic performance at the Bongo Flava@30 anniversary festival. 2Baba was among the headline performers at the festival, held on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at Eden Highlands Hotel in Mbeya, as Tanzania’s music industry marked 30 years of Bongo Flava. The Nigerian singer’s appearance added an international flavour to the celebration, which brought together some of Tanzania’s established music stars to reflect on the growth and influence of the country’s popular music genre. His performance reportedly drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, further demonstrating his appeal to music lovers beyond Nigeria. Other artistes who performed at the festival included Bongo Flava pioneers and established acts such as Mr Blue, Afande Sele, Kalapina, Juma Nature, Gangwe Mob and Chidi Benz. The festival was part of activities marking the 30-year journey of Bongo Flava, a genre that has evolved from a local Tanzanian sound into an influential force in contemporary African music. 2Baba’s participation also highlighted the growing cultural ties between Nigeria and Tanzania, particularly through music and entertainment. Widely regarded as one of Africa’s influential musicians, 2Baba has built a career spanning several decades, with hit songs that have earned him a broad following across the continent. His appearance in Mbeya further underscored the reach of Nigerian music and the growing cross-border influence of African artistes. item.title: Kaduna-Kano rail line ready for December 3 inauguration — APC
item.description: …Kano-Katsina-Maradi project reaches 70% completion The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has said the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway will be inaugurated on December 3, 2026, as the Federal Government accelerates the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria. The council also disclosed that the 203-kilometre Kaduna-Zaria-Kano railway project had reached approximately 90 per cent completion, while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project had attained 70 per cent completion. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the projects demonstrated President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to expanding railway infrastructure, improving regional connectivity and facilitating the movement of passengers and goods. It said the Kano-Katsina-Maradi project was barely five per cent complete when Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while the Kaduna-Kano railway was less than 30 per cent complete. According to the statement, the Kaduna-Kano railway, an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line, will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano, linking major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria. The council said the two projects were recently inspected on the directive of the President by a Federal Government delegation led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi. It said Adebiyi expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation. The inspection also included a train test run from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort. The statement added that Tinubu had directed the immediate resolution of outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis to facilitate the completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano. It further disclosed that the completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section of the Kaduna-Kano railway and the 250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi project would be inaugurated on December 3, 2026. When fully operational, the Kaduna-Kano railway is expected to improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors. Similarly, the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and neighbouring Niger Republic. The council reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to completing ongoing infrastructure projects across the country in line with its development agenda. item.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: NDC questions Tinubu’s fresh approval
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has questioned the latest approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Sea Port by President Bola Tinubu, recalling that the project had earlier received approval under former President Muhammadu Buhari in December 2020. The opposition party accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of making repeated promises on the project without delivering on previous commitments, asking how many times the Federal Government would approve the same port. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the NDC recalled that the Federal Executive Council (FEC), under Buhari, had on December 16, 2020, approved the implementation of the first phase of the $4.6 billion Ibom Deep Sea Port project. It said the approval named Bollore/Power China as the preferred bidder and was intended to pave the way for the commencement of construction. The statement, titled, “APC’s Endless Lies and Deceit: How Many Times Will APC Approve Ibom Deep Sea Port?”, followed Tinubu’s announcement of approval for the proposed port during his visit to Akwa Ibom State on November 6, 2026. The NDC also recalled that Tinubu, as the APC presidential candidate, had promised to build the port during the party’s campaign rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on January 30, 2023. Quoting the President’s campaign remarks, the party said he had told supporters: “We will do mechanised farming. We will export food from Akwa Ibom. We will build your seaport.” It, however, accused the APC of failing to fulfil the promise, arguing that the latest announcement amounted to a fresh commitment on a project that had already received federal approval. “In a brazen display of ignorance of statecraft and the elevation of grand deceit as a campaign strategy, President Tinubu, as APC presidential candidate, first promised the port during his 2023 campaign,” the party said. The NDC described the latest announcement as another promise that might not be fulfilled, urging Nigerians to hold the ruling party accountable for its previous commitments. Drawing a comparison with the Federal Government’s electricity supply promises, the opposition party said residents of Akwa Ibom were still waiting for the proposed deep sea port despite the earlier approval. It also urged Nigerians to reject the APC in future elections, declaring that a new Nigeria was possible under the NDC. item.title: Dangote refinery IPO misses 10m investors target
item.description: Aliko Dangote, Chairman of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), has disclosed that the initial public offering (IPO) of the company’s refinery business failed to meet its target of attracting 10 million investors. Dangote, however, said the offer recorded participation from millions of investors, describing the level of demand as significant despite falling short of the target. He spoke at the 25th annual conference of Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) in Lagos, where he attributed the shortfall to time constraints and difficulties some prospective investors encountered in accessing the offer. The billionaire businessman said the exact number of participating investors was yet to be officially determined. “We cannot tell the figure right away because we have not reported to this, but we’ve gotten an amazing demand from various people,” he said. Comparing the level of participation with other major public offerings, Dangote said the refinery IPO had attracted millions of investors, exceeding the participation recorded in some prominent African and international offers. “If you look at it, the largest participating shareholders, like here now, was I think GTBank. When they did their own, it was 200,000. Okay, we are talking about millions of people that participated,” he said. He cited Kenya’s Safaricom offering, which attracted fewer than 900,000 investors, and Saudi Aramco’s global offering, which recorded about five million investors. “We didn’t hit the 10 million because of time constraint, and a lot of people, they didn’t know how to access,” Dangote said. He described the response as evidence of growing public confidence in investment opportunities and the capacity of African businesses to mobilise domestic capital. “But it’s the shared trust of public enterprise that we have today in Africa, and that’s why people are now beginning to remove that money under their mattresses to go and invest,” he added. The Dangote refinery IPO, tagged ‘The People’s IPO’, offered 4.1 billion shares at N525 each, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares valued at N5,250. The offer opened on September 14 and was subsequently extended to October 27. Before the offer commenced, Dangote had announced a target of 10 million retail investors as part of efforts to broaden ownership of the refinery beyond institutional and high-net-worth investors. Reuters reported that more than two million investors had subscribed through digital channels before the offer closed, while the IPO attracted about N6.4 trillion in orders from Nigerian retail and institutional investors, approximately three times the targeted offer size. Dangote had also disclosed that applications came from 120 countries, including all 54 African countries. item.title: Flamingos’ Victory Not A Fluke, Performance Reflects Years Of Development – Coach Busari
item.description: Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and tactical discipline after their impressive campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, while expressing optimism about African football’s future. Busari in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. He noted that the Flamingos had competed in a difficult group that included the defending champions, adding that the experience demonstrated the progress being made in African women’s youth football. “What we are seeing now is not a fluke. It is about development, it is about character, and it is about fighting from the beginning to really get it right. So we are elated and happy,” he said. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. ﻿ He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. He described the encounter as a tactical contest that required collective defending, discipline and effective game management. According to him, the final stages of the match presented additional challenges as fatigue and anxiety began to affect the young players. Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari celebrating the victory over Japan in the finals of the U-17 World Cup at Rabat on Saturday “The young girls are tired. We have to manage their mental scenario at that point in time. We have to manage the tactics where they need to just hustle for the ball, play fewer touches and play to the zones where the Japanese are less at home,” he explained. He identified dedication, determination and discipline as key principles that guided the team’s approach. “We need to play to our own strengths, not to the opposition’s strengths. Because if we open the game, they are quicker and they can get more one-v-ones,” he said. The coach added that the Flamingos deliberately pressed Japan to force long balls, which would give them opportunities to recover possession and launch attacks. item.title: Lagos Governorship Debate Holds At 7 P.M. Today
item.description: The Nigeria Debate Consortium, a series of debates for the 2027 general elections in Nigeria, will begin today with the Lagos governorship debate. ﻿ It is the first debate in the series, organised by the consortium, which comprises Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper, in selected battleground states ahead of the 2027 elections. The series will end with a presidential debate/townhall. ﻿ The Lagos debate will hold at 7:00 p.m. at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos State. The major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat include incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Deji Doherty of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). The organisers had earlier explained that the initiative would provide a credible, non-partisan platform for participating candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on the issues that matter most to Lagos residents. It will provide an opportunity for voters to put the candidates’ capacity, ideas and priorities — from transportation and infrastructure to security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth — under public scrutiny before the February 6, 2027, governorship elections. The major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat include incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). The Consortium assured that the debate would adhere to established professional standards, with fairness, neutrality, equal opportunity and editorial independence as guiding principles. It added that all participating candidates would be subject to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. The major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat include incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). Channels Television stated the event reflects the media’s responsibility to inform the electorate and strengthen democratic accountability. “Voters deserve more than campaign promises; they deserve clear answers, credible plans and an opportunity to assess those seeking their mandate. This debate will place issues, ideas and the future of Lagos at the centre of the electoral conversation. “Our responsibility is to help citizens make informed choices based on what candidates propose and how convincingly they demonstrate their capacity to deliver,” it added. item.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s approval of financing arrangements for the Ibom Deep Sea Port as a defining moment in the state’s economic development. He stated this in a statewide broadcast following the President’s visit to Akwa Ibom on Friday, November 6, during which he announced approval for the project. Governor Eno said the deep seaport would serve as a gateway to economic transformation, opening up opportunities in international trade, investment, industrial growth and employment. He expressed confidence that the project would reposition Akwa Ibom as a major economic and maritime hub in Nigeria and the Gulf of Guinea. Governor Eno thanked President Tinubu for his confidence in the state and commitment to national development, assuring him of the Akwa Ibom State Government’s full cooperation towards the successful realisation of the project. ﻿ He described the approval as a significant step in the state’s economic journey and said the government recognised the responsibility that came with the opportunity. The governor also commended residents for their participation in the President’s visit, noting that the reception reflected Akwa Ibom’s reputation as a peaceful, welcoming and investment-ready state. He expressed appreciation to traditional rulers, religious leaders, political stakeholders, youths, women, security agencies, public servants, students and other groups who contributed to the successful hosting of the President. On the forthcoming 2027 general election, he pledged that Akwa Ibom people would support President Tinubu at the polls on January 16, 2027, as part of efforts to ensure continuity in the administration beginning May 29, 2027. He ended the broadcast by thanking the President for his support and urging residents to remain committed to the state’s development, declaring: “Together, we will ARISE, build and prosper.” The post Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation appeared first on Channels Television .
